reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 discusses phase separation and interstitial effects in other RHEAs, not Ni doping or FCC precipitate formation. E2 notes the strength-ductility trade-off in single-phase BCC HEAs but provides no evidence that Ni additions create beneficial FCC precipitates. E3 reports creep activation energies for different alloys, unrelated to the proposed mechanism. None of the cited passages address Ni as an FCC stabilizer, its effect on ductility, irradiation defect recombination, or phase stability at 1600 °C.
premises: Adding ~3–5 at.% Ni to NbMoTaW will produce a dual-phase BCC + FCC microstructure
FCC precipitates will improve room-temperature ductility via additional slip systems
FCC precipitates will act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects, reducing damage
The BCC matrix will preserve high-temperature yield strength comparable to undoped NbMoTaW
Phase stability will be maintained up to ~1600 °C
